newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen steady, fundamentals mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen steady, fundamentals mixed.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Tuesday were expected to be little changed from Monday amid thin discussion as most traders were away for an oil conference, traders said.
Traders were mixed about near term market direction.

Some traders said India's recent tender to buy September cargoes would help to support prices. They said pockets of demand from China were also seen with bids ranging between $112 and $114 per tonne fob basis.
Others said Taiwan's tender to sell 30,000 tonnes of fuel oil for October 1-10 lifting will depress prices. They said a trader was also currently loading a cargo from South Korea.
They said the trader will be keen to see low prices. The trader told Reuters he was unsure if the cargo would eventually be brought to Singapore.
Bids/offers for 180-cst cargoes lifting in October were at $113.75/$115.50 per tonne. Levels were little changed from Monday's $114-$116.
A major was also offering October barrels. He pegged premiums at $2-$3 per tonne over Singapore quotes.
Singapore September swaps were quoted firmer at $114/$115 per tonne, fairly stable from Monday's levels.
